tellings.difference: Told firsthand by Maguire, who places it in the NSA chief scientist's office during the Clinton years as a tech-transfer meeting, where the story speaks of a White House science adviser.
tellings.link_reason: Maguire's firsthand account of a meeting with Carl Sagan. The story is Michels relaying, from Maguire, a meeting with Sagan and a White House science adviser about a Venus anomaly, so it appears to be the same meeting.

as_told.title: Carl Sagan at NSA chief scientist's tech transfer meeting

plain: A man named Bob Maguire, a contractor for the CIA, says he walked into a meeting about something strange found on Venus and knew why he was there: in the room sat the astronomer Carl Sagan, "maybe the most famous venusian planet scientist that ever lived." Michels repeats a version he heard, in which the meeting included the White House science adviser, while Maguire himself places it in the office of the chief scientist at the National Security Agency, the US government's electronic spying agency, during the Clinton years, as a meeting about passing technology on. Told either way, it would mean a top scientist was quietly brought in on an unexplained finding.
